extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on patent prosecution automation (patent attorneys, recommender/LLM system developers, and applied AI researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, evaluating, and deploying systems (recommender + LLM) to assist patent attorneys in drafting responses to Office Actions (OA), including dataset construction, embedding/extraction methods, recommendation ranking, and human evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision@k
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision@k — used to assess non-hybrid recommender systems (reported as percentages, e.g., precision@10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in the experiments (precision@10). Used to quantify how many of the top-k recommended templates are relevant; CF increases precision by recommending templates based on similar attorneys' past behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall@k
rubrics_metrics.description: Recall@k — used to assess non-hybrid recommender systems (reported as percentages, e.g., recall@10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in the experiments (recall@10). CB (content-based) tends to yield higher recall due to emphasis on document similarity and greater diversity/coverage; CF often yields lower recall because it focuses on attorney preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: nDCG@k
rubrics_metrics.description: nDCG@k — normalized discounted cumulative gain at k, reported as a percentage (e.g., nDCG@10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses ranking quality of top-k recommendations by accounting for graded relevance and position. Report alongside precision@k and recall@k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report median and mean metrics for hybrid systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For hybrid systems, report both median and mean precision@k, recall@k, and nDCG@k across all topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid-system performance is summarized by median (and mean) metrics across topics to capture topic-level variability (the paper reports median (mean) values in tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-k selection (k=10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use top-k = 10 recommended templates (k = 10) for analysis and visualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The experiments extract the top k templates T_refined,ci and use k = 10 for analyzing embedding relationships, nearest neighbors, and reporting precision/recall/nDCG@10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding extraction method choice (Sentence-BERT vs LLM embeddings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content-based (CB) embeddings can be extracted using traditional LM methods (e.g., Sentence-BERT as in PARIS) or LLM-based embeddings (e.g., GPT-3 text-embedding-ada-002 as in LE-PARIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LE-PARIS (LLM-based embeddings) demonstrated stronger semantic understanding and higher recall@10 in experiments. When documents are large, perform syntactic and semantic segmentation and then combine embeddings due to token limitations of embedding APIs/models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segmentation of large documents for embedding extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents exceed token limits, conduct syntactic and semantic segmentation and then combine their embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary for LLM-based embedding extraction (token limits); ensures representation of large OA documents by merging segment embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Filtering algorithms selection (ALS, BPR, BiVAE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use matrix factorization-based algorithms (ALS and BPR) and autoencoder algorithms (BiVAE) for CF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BPR showed superior recall@10, precision@10, and nDCG@10 in CF experiments. CF boosts precision by leveraging patterns of similar attorneys but can reduce coverage/recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tradeoff: CF precision vs CB recall
rubrics_metrics.description: CF tends to recommend templates based on past behaviors/preferences of similar attorneys (enhancing precision), while CB emphasizes document similarity (increasing diversity and recall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design hybrid systems to combine these complementary strengths to achieve both high precision and recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cascade hybrid refinement (CB+CF linear combination L(·))
rubrics_metrics.description: Refinement process that linearly combines CF-ranked templates T_cf,ci with CB-ranked templates T_cb,k ∩ T_ci via a linear combination L(·) and selects top-k from T_refined,ci.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid approach: consider topic membership and intersection between CB and CF results, using a linear combination to refine rankings and propose final recommended response templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visualization (t-SNE) to evaluate embedding distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Project embeddings (PARIS vs LE-PARIS) into a 3D t-SNE space to examine clustering patterns and the distance relationship between a received OA and its top-k embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARIS (Sentence-BERT) embeddings appeared dispersed without a clear pattern; LE-PARIS embeddings were more clustered, indicating stronger semantic understanding. Visualization supports qualitative assessment of embedding quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM response-generation quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate generated OA responses on readability/structure, legal-argument depth, specific claim references, technical explanation, and hallucination risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed model behaviors: PatentGPT-J-6B often created continuous text blocks with repetition and limited legal depth; Llama 2 improved structure and technical rebuttal but may hallucinate; GPT-3.5 focused on term elucidation and adaptability; GPT-4 provided comprehensive coverage, suggested claim amendments, balanced legal/technical strategies, and used placeholders to reduce hallucination risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generating patent claims with LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: The system should not attempt to create patent claims (claims are prone to hallucinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, use LLMs to argue technical differences between the current case and prior art, where LLMs' strengths in discerning differences can be leveraged safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-shot evaluation protocol for LLM generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a zero-shot evaluation by inputting a specific OA segment (e.g., 35 U.S.C. § 102 text + examiner statements) together with role instructions (assume role of a patent attorney) and analyze generated outcomes qualitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used here as a preliminary qualitative investigation; follow up with domain-expert quantitative evaluations (Study 5) for more rigorous assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation: blind A/B testing with domain experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct blind testing where patent attorneys are randomly assigned outputs from different LLMs, unaware of the source, and rate satisfaction on a 1-5 star scale guided by 'Are you satisfied with the generated result?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each attorney received ten results from each LLM; blind/random assignment reduces bias. Use repeated measures designs when multiple ratings per rater are gathered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis for within-subject LLM comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply repeated measures ANOVA to test differences between generation methods, followed by post hoc paired t-tests with correction for multiple comparisons (False Discovery Rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report F-statistic, p-values, and effect size (e.g., η²_p). In the study, generation methods accounted for 93% of variance (η²_p = .93). Use FDR or similar adjustments for multiple pairwise tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal performance analysis using mixed linear models (MLM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mixed linear models to predict attorney performance from system engagement over time, accounting for repeated observations and random effects (attorney and time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control for demographics (gender, age, education, tenure), attorney (subject) random effects, and time effects. Compare model fit (e.g., -2 log-likelihood) between fixed-effects and mixed-effects models to justify MLM choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of engagement with systems (PARIS / LE-PARIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement measured as the number of times the system was fully utilized (from entry to completion of the response draft with system assistance), weighted by the depth of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this weighted count as the predictor in MLMs to associate system engagement with attorney performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of attorney performance on OA tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance measured as monthly OA workload adjusted for difficulty by an impartial third party responsible for task assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use difficulty-adjusted monthly workload as the dependent variable in longitudinal models to assess practical impact of system engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include demographic/control covariates
rubrics_metrics.description: Control variables to include gender (coding specified: 1 = female, 0 = male), age, education level, and tenure (measured in months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these as fixed effects in MLMs to isolate the effect of system engagement on performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and interpret effect sizes and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report coefficients, standard errors, p-values, and effect sizes (e.g., η²_p) when presenting statistical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PARIS engagement coefficient = .086 (SE = .012, p < .01); LE-PARIS engagement coefficient = .162 (SE = .014, p < .01). Use -2 log-likelihood comparisons to assess model fit improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset construction and curation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a historical database of OA responses; use topic modeling and extensive expert consensus for iterative database refinement to ensure quality and categorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Database construction is nascent—future work should expand and refine using tailored language models, improved tokenization, and iterative expert review to improve OA/response semantic capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future methodological recommendations for recommender components
rubrics_metrics.description: For CB: train embedding models specifically on OA/response data rather than off-the-shelf extractors. For CF: experiment with contrastive or generative self-supervised recommenders and data augmentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also explore LLMs-as-recommenders and alternative hybrid strategies; these are suggested directions rather than evaluated standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and ethical guideline for LLM use in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious of intellectual property and client confidentiality risks when using LLMs for OA response drafting; compliance with professional confidentiality rules (e.g., ABA Rule 1.6) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and firms should consider using locally run, open-sourced LLMs instead of external APIs to mitigate risks of leaking confidential prosecution information.
